text:
sam: Quick flag - the /v1/uploads API reference currently shows only a JSON/base64 payload. I tried the example and got 415 Unsupported Media Type from hosted.

sam: Broken example in PR:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{\"filename\":\"pic.png\",\"file\":\"<base64>\"}'
```

diana: Thanks for catching. Canonical for hosted should be multipart/form-data. We should update the OpenAPI requestBody to accept both media types (oneOf) but render multipart examples first. Move the JSON/base64 snippet to an "Alternate (legacy)" box.

kevin: I'll patch the docs PR. Plan: OpenAPI -> requestBody oneOf [multipart/form-data, application/json]; examples under each; multipart-first examples for cURL, python requests, node fetch; SDK convenience snippet for JS/Python/Ruby.

kevin: Multipart cURL I'll add:
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -F "file=@./pic.png" \n  -F "filename=pic.png"
# curl will set Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=... automatically
```

sanjay: Confirming runtime: Hosted requires multipart/form-data for uploads. Dedicated/Private can accept JSON/base64 only if the deployment enables the legacy_uploads toggle. Also: hosted max file size = 25 MB; Dedicated is customer-configurable.

diana: Add a one-liner migration note: "If you previously used JSON/base64, switch to multipart; SDKs automatically pick multipart when given a file path/stream." Also suggest streaming for large files to avoid buffering.

sam: SDK snippet examples to include (short):
JS SDK convenience:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk'
const client = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_KEY)
await client.uploadFile({ path: './pic.png', filename: 'pic.png' })
```
Python client convenience:
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = c.upload_file(path='pic.png', filename='pic.png')
print(resp['id'])
```
Ruby example (convenience wrapper):
```ruby
client = Redwood::Client.new(ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'])
client.upload_file(path: 'pic.png', filename: 'pic.png')
```

kevin: Also including a short Node fetch manual multipart example for users not using SDKs:
```js
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', fs.createReadStream('./pic.png'));
form.append('filename', 'pic.png');
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}` }, body: form });
```

diana: For Go we should show streaming with multipart.Writer and io.Copy to avoid loading file into memory. Add a note about 413 for >25 MB on hosted and retry/backoff for 429.

sanjay: I'll review the PR wording around the legacy_uploads flag to ensure we don't accidentally imply hosted accepts JSON. Also confirm exact config name for Dedicated toggles.

kevin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1250 (WIP) includes OpenAPI change + examples + migration note. Preview link once built.

docs-preview-bot: Preview deployed for PR 1250 https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr/1250/uploads-media-types. Please verify examples, the legacy callout, and max file size note.

diana: Preview looks good. Two tiny nits: 1) explicitly call out `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` in the cURL example comment even though curl sets it, 2) add a short server error example for payload >25MB (HTTP 413).

sam: I'll add the 413 example and a short tip: "If files are near the limit, recommend chunking or direct-object-storage presigned uploads (link to Storage guide)."

kevin: Added fixes and assigned reviews: diana (docs), sanjay (technical), sam (SDK samples). Will merge after approvals. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks all 44d
